TextBlock.TextLine: Public Advertiser, Friday May 10, 1765, [p.2]
A few Observations on the Pictures at Spring
Gardens.
Mr. HAMILTON, at Rome.
No. 46. Achilles lamenting the Death of Pa-
troclus.-Great Encouragement should be given
to those Painters, who cultivate the nobler
Provinces of Art, and endeavour to touch
the Passions by historical or poetical Pieces,
rather than to sacrifice to the Vanity of Man-
king by Portrait-Painting. The Piece before
us is not without Merit, but the Legs of Pa-
troclus de not appear like those of a dead
Man. Perhaps it would be impossible for
those of a dead Person to be in that Position,
in which the Picture represents those of Pa-
troclus.
Mr. HAYMAN, in St. Martin's Lane.
48. Sigismunda.-A very woeful Picture!,
very sad indeed!
49. Falstaff recruiting.-Falstaff the worst
Figure in the Piece. Shallow the best.-This
is a favourite Subject of Mr. H's.
Hayman, dull Mannerist!
Mr. HONE, St. James's Place.
CHURCHILL.
52. Portrait of a Gentleman.-An excellent
Portrait.
53. Ditto.-Ditto.
54. Ditto of a Lady.-This is the Portrait
of a Lady, whose Charms are well known to the
Team. The Painter has ingeniously attempted
to acquaint us with her Name by a Rebus
upon Canvas. By her Side a Kitten [KITTY]
is attempting to get into a Bason of Gold Fish
[KITTY FISH-]-what Pity it is, he did not
make the Rebus complete, and, according to
Subtle in the Alchemist, place on the other
Side a Dog snarling-er-KITTY FISH--ER!
Mr. GEORGE JAMES, Dean-Street, Soho.
57. Whole Length of a Lady.-A Piece of
great Merit. This is not the first excellent Pro-
duction which we have seen from the Hand of
Mr. James.
Mr. KETTLE, Great Queen-Street, Lin-
64. Portrait of a Lady, whole Length.-This
coln's Inn-Fields.
is intended to represent Mrs. Yates in the
Character of Mandane, in the Orphan of
China; but Mr. Kettle has by no Means done
Justice to the Beauty of Mrs. Yates.-This
Kettle is just the Opposite of the Kettle of Medea
which renewed Youth; for the Copy appears
twenty Years older than the Original.
Mr. HENRY LEAKE, Leicester-Fields.
73. Mr. Powell, in the Character of Posthumus.
A good Likeness of Mr. Powell. I think,
however, the Character of Posthumus might
have afforded some more interesting Crisis,
some picturesque Moment of Passion, in the
3^d or Last Act of the Play of Cymbeline.
Mr. PENNY, Mortimer-Street.
96. An officer relieving a sick Soldier.-The
sick Soldier and his Family are happily ima-
gined, and well executed. The Officer, which
seems intended for the Marquis of Granby, not
so well.
97. The Return from a Fair.-A natural Scene,
somewhat in the Manner of Hogarth.
Mr. WEST, Castle-Street.
There is great Delicacy both in the Idea
and Execution of this Painter's Pieces. But
there is a Glow in his Colouring which gives
a Kind of unnatural Varnish to his Pictures.
There seems also to be a Sameness in his Fi-
gures, which, if not carefully avoided, will
obtain the Artist the Name of a Mannerist.
Perhaps also they are too delicate. It is dan-
gerous to attempt to exhibit Forms more beauti-
ful than those of Nature.
Mr. ZAFFANIS, Lincoln's-Inn-Fields.
